research_rationale:
Executive Order 13882 of July 26, 2019 (84 FR 37055), Blocking Property and Suspending Entry of Certain Persons Contributing to the Situation in Mali, declares a national emergency and orders ten sections. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13882.txt, 84 FR 37055, PDF pages 1-4) carries the heading, the date July 26, 2019 and FR Doc. 2019-16383. The dossier inventory has 25 clauses covering the declaration of emergency, section 1 (blocking and its criteria), section 2 (suspension of entry), section 3 (donations), section 4 (what the prohibitions include), section 5 (evasion and conspiracy), section 6 (definitions), section 7 (no prior notice), section 8 (delegation to the Treasury), section 9 (authority to submit congressional reports) and section 10 (general provisions); it is accepted. The order states no end date or condition. The emergency continues under the National Emergencies Act by annual notice, the last held notice being that of July 21, 2026. The Mali Sanctions Regulations (31 CFR part 555) implement the order. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13882 (19 files) finds the order, the regulations rule and its CFR codification, and the seven continuation notices; none revokes, supersedes or amends it. The status on 2026-10-14 is operative for all 25 clauses. Section 9's authorization to submit the recurring and final reports is a standing authorization, not a one-time command, and continues while the emergency does. The held text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF; page images were not inspected.
